solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Possibly mums of kids who use potty having to remove clothes endlessly

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the preceding words are scrambled madly into a new order
without ends means both the first and last letters of the word are dropped

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be scrambled
to divest is to strip off clothing

explanation.surface: Mothers of potty-training toddlers keep having to take their children's clothes off.
explanation.walkthrough: HOUSEWIVES is defined by example: many mothers of small children are housewives, hence 'Possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who run a home rather than going out to work, often caring for young children, are a typical example.

clue.text: Put away wine by small measures

blocks.note: in. is the abbreviation for inches, small units of length
hock is German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: Someone drinks up a glass of wine a little at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' reads as drinking, but means pawned; the clue's order is reversed, with 'by' placing the wine beside the measures.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods pawned at a pawnshop are said to be in hock until redeemed, so they are stored as security.

clue.text: Let’s split

blocks.note: first meaning: to hire out property for payment
second meaning: torn apart, past tense of rend

explanation.walkthrough: 'Let's split' sounds like slang for leaving together; the 's is just 'is' joining two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent is the verb for hiring out a property, and rent is also the past participle of rend, meaning torn apart.

clue.text: Turning it completed material for aircraft manufacture

indicators.note: turning round makes the following short word run back to front
completing a chemical symbol means writing out the full name of the element it stands for

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Spinning something until finished produces a material for building aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: TI is the chemical symbol for TITANIUM, so turning 'it' gives the symbol and completing it spells out the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanium is a light, strong metal widely used in airframes and jet engines, so it is an example of aerospace material.

clue.text: Enthusiastic half of 19 turned up

indicators.note: half of means only the first portion of that other entry is used
in a down entry, turned up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the first half of the answer to 19 across

explanation.surface: Keen on half of the earlier entry flipped upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 19 across is DIVAGATE; its first four letters, written upwards, give AVID.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid describes someone keen and eager, a straightforward synonym for being very keen about something.

clue.text: Condemn opera penned by numskull

indicators.note: penned by means shut inside, so the first item sits within the second

blocks.note: a dunce is a stupid person
ENO is English National Opera

explanation.surface: A critic attacks an opera written by an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opera' tempts you towards NOH, the Japanese drama, but the London company abbreviation is what fits.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce is to publicly declare something wrong, a direct synonym for strong public criticism.

clue.text: Call up girl with fine heart

indicators.note: the word for fine becomes the heart of the name, so it sits in its middle

blocks.note: a girl's name
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Phoning a young woman who has a good heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine heart' suggests a kindly nature; really OK goes into the heart of EVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to summon a memory or feeling to mind, the same as calling it up.

clue.text: Fashionable opening design

blocks.note: what is in is in fashion
a vent is an opening for air or gas

explanation.surface: A stylish new launch for a fashion design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' looks like a launch party; here it is a hole, and 'design' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To design something is to create or devise it for the first time, which is what inventing means.

clue.text: Unopened posy with, for example, an unusual bouquet

indicators.note: unopened means the word loses its opening letter
unusual signals that the gathered letters are put into a strange new order

blocks.note: taken as written, before losing its first letter
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Comparing a closed-up posy with an exotic bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unopened' sounds like flower buds, but it just removes the first letter of posy.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small bunch of sweet-smelling flowers, a dated synonym for a little posy or bouquet.

clue.text: Defeat explanation that’s no good

indicators.note: 'that's no' means the thing named next is taken away from the word

blocks.note: a gloss is an explanatory note on a text
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Excusing a defeat with an account that doesn't hold up.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss is a game or battle not won, so it is a direct synonym for being beaten.

clue.text: Bizarre old aunt thrashed his bum

indicators.note: something thrashed is beaten about, so those letters are knocked into a new order
bum means bad or faulty, so the word before it is wrongly arranged

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange scene: an elderly aunt spanking a boy's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' reads as a body part being spanked, but it is a second anagram signal meaning faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlandish means strikingly odd or unfamiliar, a straight synonym for strange or weird.

clue.text: Break a new, weaker, spring again

indicators.note: to break something is to smash it apart so its letters can be reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written

explanation.surface: Breaking in a replacement spring that's less strong than the old one.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring here means come back to life, as nature does in spring, so springing again is waking once more.

clue.text: Battery chickens are originally put in another bird’s brood

indicators.note: originally means only the opening letter of each of those words counts
put in means placed inside the next item

blocks.note: a nid or nide is a brood of pheasants
first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Battery hens' eggs being slipped into a different bird's nest, cuckoo-style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battery chickens' is a familiar phrase, but 'Battery' alone is the definition. A NICAD is a nickel-cadmium rechargeable cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicad is a rechargeable nickel-cadmium cell, so it is a type of electric power source.

clue.text: Hiding drug in prison after one gets a potentially long stretch

indicators.note: hiding something means keeping it concealed inside another thing
after places the prison part behind the single letter

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
a cage confines like a prison
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone caught smuggling drugs into jail gets a long sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long stretch' sounds like a prison term; it is really a long era of glaciation. E goes after the C of CAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice age is a geological period of extensive glaciation that can last many thousands of years.

clue.text: Overdo rising electronic levy, ultimately embedded in rhythmic music

indicators.note: only the final letter of the levy is lodged inside the music
in a down answer, rising means everything reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic
TAX, a levy, minus its last letter, which moves into the music
REGGAE, the Jamaican style, with the X of TAX lodged before its final letter

explanation.surface: Going over the top about a new e-tax on reggae music.
explanation.walkthrough: E-TAX and REGGAE run together, but the X of TAX shifts to sit just before the last E of REGGAE; the whole string then reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To exaggerate is to overstate or overemphasise something, which is what overdoing it means.

clue.text: Unhappy business guild invested in capital

blocks.note: livery is an old word for irritable or liverish
a company is a business

explanation.surface: A disgruntled trade association that has put its money into capital investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in capital' sounds financial, but means formally established in the capital: livery companies are the ancient trade guilds of the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery companies are London's historic trade associations, chartered bodies whose members wore distinctive dress or livery.

clue.text: Old German noble without a degree

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the title wraps around the qualification

blocks.note: a lord is a nobleman
MBA is a Master of Business Administration degree

explanation.surface: An aristocrat from old Germany who never went to university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking a degree; here it means outside, wrapped around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lombards were a Germanic people who invaded and ruled much of Italy in the early Middle Ages.

clue.text: Droll, almost vacuous, given time to be meditative

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter of that word is cut

blocks.note: rum means odd or comical
inane means empty or silly
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A funny but rather empty-headed person, given some time, becomes thoughtful.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum is British for odd or peculiar. The adjective ruminant, like a cow chewing the cud, means given to musing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruminant as an adjective means contemplative, from ruminating, pondering over and over like an animal chewing cud.

clue.text: Old master requires whole bible for a 17

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
MA is a Master of Arts
a sum is a total

explanation.surface: An old master demands an entire Bible for an assignment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bible' reads as scripture, but bible is an old name for this stomach, for its leaf-like folds; 17 is RUMINANT.
explanation.definitionFit: The omasum, the third chamber of a cud-chewer's stomach, is also called the bible or psalterium because its folds resemble pages.

clue.text: Digress from scandal concerning famous prima donna?

blocks.note: a diva is a celebrated female opera singer
-gate is the suffix for a scandal, after Watergate

explanation.surface: Changing the subject away from the gossip about a celebrity soprano.
explanation.walkthrough: The scandal suffix -gate follows the subject it concerns, so DIVA comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To divagate is to wander off course or stray from the subject, a formal word for wandering off topic.

clue.text: Even Etonians admit “some Europeans will live here”

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the answer is held inside those words

blocks.note: spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Even old boys of Eton concede that Europeans will settle somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Veneto is a region of north-east Italy, around Venice, so it is a place where Italians reside.

clue.text: Mark, say, plough in the Dales?

blocks.note: first meaning: the pen name of the American author Samuel Clemens, whose first name here is Mark
second meaning: the Plough is also Charles's Wain, and in Yorkshire dialect 'the' becomes t'

explanation.walkthrough: The Dales are in Yorkshire, where 'the' is clipped to t'. A wain is a farm wagon, and the Plough constellation is also called Charles's Wain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain is the pen name of the American novelist, while Yorkshire speech would call the Wain 't'wain'.

clue.text: In a fight, beginning to take on a rugby team

indicators.note: the beginning of a word means only its first letter is taken

blocks.note: warring means fighting
first letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A brawling player takes on a rugby side.
explanation.walkthrough: Warrington Wolves are a rugby league club from Warrington in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Warrington is a Cheshire town whose rugby league club is usually just called by the town's name.

clue.text: Primarily reckless and soft-headed

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so each word gives only its opening letter

blocks.note: first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone who is mainly careless and foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: being mainly reckless and soft-headed is a fair description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash means acting hastily without thought for consequences, which combines being heedless and foolish.

clue.text: Patch up date, maybe after one’s done a bunk

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the letters read from bottom to top
doing a bunk means running off, so the letter for one disappears

blocks.note: a date is an example of a fruit
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone tries to fix a romantic date after their partner has run off.
explanation.walkthrough: To do a bunk is British slang for running away. Patch here is a noun, a patch of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Turf is a piece of grass-covered ground, and one's own patch is one's territory or turf.

clue.text: Study what follows 18 in a 17

blocks.note: first meaning: to learn a subject, as at university
second meaning: the fourth stomach of a ruminant, which comes after the omasum

explanation.walkthrough: 18 is OMASUM and 17 is RUMINANT; the next chamber is the abomasum, whose old name is the read or reed.
explanation.definitionFit: Read means to study a subject at university, and is also a dialect name for the rennet-stomach of cattle.

clue.text: Hardly any particular aspect held back inventor

indicators.note: held back means the phrase is read backwards

blocks.note: no as in 'no great amount'
a side is one aspect of something

explanation.surface: Having barely any distinctive quality kept a certain inventor in obscurity.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas EDISON, the American inventor of the phonograph and an electric light bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the prolific American who devised the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: Joking about answer, taking turns

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the joking word goes around the letter

blocks.note: rotting is British slang for talking rubbish or joking
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Kidding around about the right answer while players take it in turns.
explanation.walkthrough: Rot means nonsense, so to be rotting is to tease or talk in jest.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotating means alternating in sequence, with each person doing a duty in turn.
